title: Learn Logging and Observability in Go
description: Instrument a Go service with useful logs, secure context, metrics, alerts, profiles, and traces.

lessons.title: Welcome to Logging and Telemetry
lessons.instruction: Telemetry should help you detect a problem and then diagnose it. Complete the two operational goals printed by this first Linko check.

lessons.title: Linko Overview
lessons.instruction: Linko is a URL shortener: a short path resolves to a stored destination and returns a redirect. Correct the destination without changing the request path.

lessons.title: What Is Observability?
lessons.instruction: Observability infers a system's internal state from its outputs. Include the signal that reveals where runtime resources are being spent.

lessons.title: Logging in Go
lessons.instruction: A log.Logger writes through an io.Writer and can own a stable prefix. Configure this logger for the Linko service.

lessons.title: Use the Logger
lessons.instruction: Pass the logger to the code that owns the event. Record the short path selected by the redirect handler.

lessons.title: Logging Requests
lessons.instruction: A useful request record includes the method, route, and final status after the handler completes. Fix the recorded redirect status.

lessons.title: Global Logger vs. Dependency Injection
lessons.instruction: Injected loggers keep configuration isolated and make components easy to test. Give the API and worker their own prefixes.

lessons.title: Logger Configuration
lessons.instruction: Set destinations and flags at the composition root so records stay consistent. Use the required service prefix without timestamps.

lessons.title: Logger Failure
lessons.instruction: A destination can fail. Logger.Output returns the writer error, so check it when losing the record matters.

lessons.title: Buffered Logging
lessons.instruction: Buffering reduces writes but delays visibility. Flush before reporting the final byte count.

lessons.title: Logger Cleanup
lessons.instruction: Shutdown must flush buffered records before closing their destination. Correct the cleanup order.

lessons.title: Structured Logging
lessons.instruction: Structured records keep a stable event name and searchable fields. Emit the link-created event with its slug.

lessons.title: Slog Package
lessons.instruction: A slog.Logger sends records through a Handler. Build the expected INFO record with a text handler.

lessons.title: Log Levels
lessons.instruction: A minimum level removes lower-priority records before they reach the sink. Raise this handler to WARN.

lessons.title: More Log Levels
lessons.instruction: A slog.LevelVar lets configuration change the threshold safely at runtime. Set it to ERROR before writing both records.

lessons.title: Key-Value Pairs
lessons.instruction: Typed slog attributes make field names and values explicit. Correct the redirect's status attribute.

lessons.title: Output Formats
lessons.instruction: JSON preserves types and nesting for collectors. Replace the human-oriented text handler with the JSON handler.

lessons.title: Best Practices
lessons.instruction: Prefer a stable event name plus the field an operator will search. Replace the vague narration with the completed Linko event.

lessons.title: Timestamps
lessons.instruction: Use one machine-readable UTC timestamp from the logging pipeline. Convert the fixed event time to UTC RFC3339.

lessons.title: Minimal Logging
lessons.instruction: Keep only fields that help investigate the failed request. Remove the request body from the operational record.

lessons.title: Redundant Logs
lessons.instruction: Repeated records inflate volume and confuse incident counts. Let only the boundary that handles the failure log it.

lessons.title: One Log Per Event
lessons.instruction: Keep an event's fields together so a collector cannot split their meaning. Print one complete redirect record.

lessons.title: Logging Errors
lessons.instruction: Log an error where it is handled and include the failed operation. Add the lookup operation to the record.

lessons.title: Stack Traces
lessons.instruction: Stack traces are useful for unexpected failures but expensive and noisy everywhere. Capture callers only at the selected error boundary.

lessons.title: Slog Groups
lessons.instruction: Groups namespace related attributes and prevent key collisions. Put the error code and kind under the error object.

lessons.title: Handle Errors Once
lessons.instruction: A layer should either add context and return an error or handle and log it. Remove the inner log so one failure creates one record.

lessons.title: Adding Attributes
lessons.instruction: Logger.With adds context shared by later records. Derive a request logger that carries the service and request ID.

lessons.title: Multiple Errors
lessons.instruction: errors.Join preserves independent failures from one operation. Join both cleanup errors so errors.Is can find each cause.

lessons.title: Logging Context
lessons.instruction: Context carries request-scoped values and cancellation, but logs should extract only approved fields. Read the request ID from the context.

lessons.title: Build Information
lessons.instruction: Version and commit fields identify the code serving an event. Correct the deployed commit while keeping the version stable.

lessons.title: Instance Context
lessons.instruction: Instance and region fields distinguish replicas during a partial failure. Select the affected Linko instance.

lessons.title: Request Context
lessons.instruction: A request record needs a correlation ID and stable route data. Correct the request ID without logging query parameters.

lessons.title: User Context
lessons.instruction: Use a stable internal user ID for correlation; avoid email addresses and other personal data. Emit only the approved identifier.

lessons.title: HTTP Error Responses
lessons.instruction: Clients need a safe message and a request ID, while internal details stay in logs. Replace the leaked database error.

lessons.title: Inter-Process Context
lessons.instruction: Correlation survives a service boundary only when it is propagated. Set the request ID header before the downstream call.

lessons.title: Log Storage
lessons.instruction: Containerized services normally write events to stdout and let the platform collect them. Select the sink used by Linko's container.

lessons.title: Logging to the Console
lessons.instruction: Keep normal events on stdout and process diagnostics on stderr. Route each fixed message to its intended buffer.

lessons.title: Filesystem Logging
lessons.instruction: File logging must handle creation, writes, and close errors. Write the expected record and read it back from a temporary file.

lessons.title: Log Rotation
lessons.instruction: Rotate before the next record would exceed the configured file limit. Fix the decision for an 80-byte file and 25-byte record.

lessons.title: Syslog
lessons.instruction: Syslog's PRI combines facility times eight plus severity. Encode local0 facility 16 with error severity 3.

lessons.title: Can You Keep a Secret?
lessons.instruction: Passwords, tokens, and private keys must never reach a log sink. Replace the token value before rendering the record.

lessons.title: Error Responses
lessons.instruction: Public errors should reveal neither stack paths nor database details. Return a generic message with the correlation ID.

lessons.title: Minimal Logging
lessons.instruction: Data minimization limits breach impact. Keep the operational status and request ID, not the submitted URL.

lessons.title: Obfuscation
lessons.instruction: Masking reduces casual exposure but is not encryption. Preserve only the final four digits needed for support.

lessons.title: Filtering Logs
lessons.instruction: Redact centrally before every handler writes. Use ReplaceAttr to filter the token attribute while preserving other fields.

lessons.title: Encrypted Logs
lessons.instruction: Encryption protects stored bytes but does not replace filtering or access control. Complete the AES-GCM round trip; production must use a unique nonce for every message.

lessons.title: Metrics
lessons.instruction: Counters grow, gauges move both ways, and histograms group observations. Correct the type chosen for request duration.

lessons.title: Prometheus
lessons.instruction: Prometheus scrapes a text exposition endpoint. Emit the HELP, TYPE, and sample lines for Linko's redirect counter.
lessons.expected:
# HELP linko_redirects_total Completed redirects.
# TYPE linko_redirects_total counter
linko_redirects_total 7

lessons.title: System Metrics
lessons.instruction: System metrics reveal utilization and saturation around the service. Report the fixed CPU, memory, and goroutine snapshot.

lessons.title: Metrics Exporters
lessons.instruction: An exporter translates another system's statistics into Prometheus samples. Convert the fixture's open-connection count.

lessons.title: What to Measure
lessons.instruction: For request-driven services, rate, errors, and duration expose user impact. Calculate the error ratio from two failures in one hundred requests.

lessons.title: Visualizing Metrics
lessons.instruction: Match the view to the question: trends use time series, one current value uses a stat, and distributions use histograms.

lessons.title: Service Metrics
lessons.instruction: Track traffic, failures, latency, and work in progress together. Apply the completed redirect to this fixed service snapshot.

lessons.title: Custom Metrics
lessons.instruction: Custom metrics should answer a product question with bounded labels. Count created links by plan, never by user ID.

lessons.title: Custom Visualizations
lessons.instruction: A useful visualization applies the right aggregation and unit. Average the fixed redirect-latency samples in milliseconds.

lessons.title: Status Code Bars
lessons.instruction: Group status codes into bounded families for a readable bar chart. Count the fixed responses as 2xx, 4xx, and 5xx.

lessons.title: Alerting
lessons.instruction: Alert on a sustained user-impacting condition rather than one noisy sample. Require all three error-ratio samples to exceed five percent.

lessons.title: Actionable Alerts
lessons.instruction: An actionable alert states impact, ownership, and where to investigate. Add the missing runbook to the Linko alert.

lessons.title: Alert Thresholds
lessons.instruction: A window prevents a single spike from flapping the alert. Fire only after three consecutive values exceed 80.

lessons.title: Profiling
lessons.instruction: Profile before optimizing: CPU finds hot execution, heap finds retained memory, and goroutine profiles find blocked concurrency. Correct the symptom mapping.

lessons.title: Integrating pprof
lessons.instruction: Importing net/http/pprof registers method-aware diagnostic routes on the default mux. Verify the GET index route; expose it only on a protected admin listener.

lessons.title: CPU Profiling
lessons.instruction: CPU profiles sample executing code during a bounded interval. Capture a short profile and confirm that pprof wrote profile bytes.

lessons.title: CPU Profiling Quiz
lessons.instruction: Choose a CPU profile when latency rises with saturated CPU and you need the hottest functions. Correct the selected artifact.

lessons.title: Memory Profiling
lessons.instruction: The heap profile reports live allocations after garbage collection context is considered. Look up the runtime's heap profile.

lessons.title: Memory Profiling Quiz
lessons.instruction: Use inuse_space for retained-memory growth and alloc_space for allocation churn. Fix the two diagnostic choices.

lessons.title: Goroutine Profiling
lessons.instruction: A goroutine profile reveals blocked stacks and leaks. Start one controlled blocked goroutine and confirm the runtime count increases.

lessons.title: Tracing
lessons.instruction: A trace is a tree of timed spans for one request. Connect the database lookup span to its HTTP parent.

lessons.title: Installing Jaeger
lessons.instruction: Jaeger receives and displays traces for this course. Run Check to verify the metrics, dashboard, and tracing services are all responding.

lessons.expected: PASS · The live observability services are ready.

lessons.title: Request Tracing
lessons.instruction: W3C traceparent carries version, trace ID, parent span ID, and flags. Extract the trace ID from the incoming header.

lessons.title: Instrumenting Traces
lessons.instruction: Tracing setup needs an exporter, service resource, and shutdown path. Complete the local provider configuration lifecycle.

lessons.title: Adding Spans
lessons.instruction: Create spans around meaningful operations, not every function. Make the Linko lookup a child of the request span.

lessons.title: Reading Traces
lessons.instruction: The longest child on the request's critical path is the first investigation target. Find it in the fixed span durations.

lessons.title: Distributed Tracing
lessons.instruction: Distributed traces remain connected only when clients inject and servers extract the same trace context. Propagate the traceparent header.
